chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Jameela, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves the bashful one, the forbearing one.

key_terms.الْحَلِيمَ: The forbearing, patient, or gentle one
key_terms.الْحَيِيَّ: The modest, bashful, or shy one (in a positive, virtuous sense)
key_terms.عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic (an honorific title for Allah)

ai.seo_question: What character traits does Allah love according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS), situating it within the chapter on forbearance to emphasize that modesty (hayaa') and gentleness (hilm) are not merely social virtues but beloved traits in the sight of Allah. This hadith serves as a foundational ethical principle in Shia moral theology, linking inner character refinement directly to divine affection and spiritual proximity.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abu Jameela, 
(It has been narrated) from Jabir, from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Loves the bashful one, the forbearing one’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Ali ibn al-Hakam from abu Jamilah from Jabir from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, loves the living person who is forbearing.”
